turns.content: Count the total outcomes as ordered five-card sequences while retaining favorable outcomes as unordered hands.
How many ways can exactly three of the four kings be selected?
Count the favorable hands containing exactly three kings and exactly two of the four queens.
Form the probability as the favorable-hand count divided by the total-hand count.
Verify that the favorable and total counts use the same unordered five-card sample space and that the favorable count enforces exactly three kings and two queens.
Report the exact ratio and its decimal value.
